summary: Mt. Hood NF L-4 cab site on Buck Peak, Hood River County: 1933 construction, register says erected 1934, gone by 1950; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Gone by 1950, per the register and firelookout.com.

events.note: Pack train carrying lumber for lookout house construction went off a ledge, August 27, 1933.
Panorama photos of the Buck Peak Lookout taken November 9, 1933.
Register says the USFS erected an L-4 cab on this site. Newspaper-era items suggest construction was underway in 1933.
Gone by 1950 per the register and firelookout.com.

evidence.supports: Location in the Mount Hood region
County is Hood River County, Oregon
Register dates L-4 cab erection to 1934
evidence.quote: In 1934, the USFS erected an L-4 cab on this site.
Panorama photos taken by Lester Moe & Reino Sarlin.

evidence.supports: Pack train carrying lumber for lookout house construction, August 1933

evidence.supports: Horse shot after pack train accident

evidence.supports: Site in Mt. Hood National Forest

corrections.why: Neither the register page nor firelookout.com gives a height for this site. No cached source supports the 3.7 m value.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts items show a pack train hauling lookout lumber in August 1933 and a panorama of the Buck Peak Lookout on November 9, 1933. The register says the USFS erected the L-4 cab in 1934. The story reports both and does not choose one.

The register and Forest Lookouts page give Hood River County. The Forest Fire Lookout Association Oregon list gives 'Hood River/ Multnomah'. The story uses Hood River County and notes the list's entry.

sources.title: Buck Peak Lookout Site (Hood River County)

notes_for_editor: Built date conflict: 1933 construction items versus the register's 1934 erection. Gone by 1950 is consistent across two sources. The brief's height_m 3.7 has no source. Other Buck Peak sites exist (a Klamath County tower on the firelookout.org list, and a southern Oregon site on the Forest Lookouts pages); keep them out. No source describes the site today.
